# BIYY Tech

> BIYY Tech builds dashboards and databases for small and medium businesses in
> Malaysia and Singapore. Two products are live: Dashboards & Databases, which
> replaces the spreadsheets a business runs on with a real database and an
> industry-specific dashboard, and Website & Integrations, which builds a new
> website for the business and wires it into that database. A third, Data &
> Intelligence, is in limited beta.

Pricing is a flat monthly fee per outlet. There is no per-transaction charge,
no implementation fee, and no annual lock-in required to start. A typical
rollout takes two weeks. Businesses whose source spreadsheets carry years of
accumulated inconsistency are quoted three to four weeks up front.

## Products

- [Dashboards & Databases](https://yiy.tech/products/dashboards): the core
  product. A database designed around how the business actually records work,
  rather than a spreadsheet copied into SQL, with dashboards laid out for the
  industry: retail, distribution, clinics, salons, tuition centres, property
  agencies, e-commerce and multi-branch groups. Every figure is live rather
  than a periodic export. Roles and permissions, so a branch manager sees their
  branch and the owner sees all of it. Forms and mobile entry replace shared
  files. Full record history and an audit trail showing who changed what and
  when. Migration from the customer's existing spreadsheets, including
  duplicate and inconsistent data, which is flagged for the customer to decide
  rather than guessed at. Export to Excel and CSV at any time.
  The distinction from a BI tool is that a BI tool draws charts over whatever
  it is fed and inherits every duplicate and stale export; BIYY replaces the
  source with a constrained database and reads the dashboard from that.
  Explicitly not offered: replacing an accounting package, enterprise data
  warehouses or streaming pipelines, dashboards built over a spreadsheet the
  customer keeps maintaining by hand, and machine learning on a few hundred
  rows.
- [Website & Integrations](https://yiy.tech/products/website): BIYY Tech designs
  and builds new websites for its customers and wires them into the database.
  The build is bespoke rather than templated, with copy written in a session
  with the business. The value to the customer is that the site takes orders
  and enquiries outside trading hours, answers the questions that otherwise
  arrive by phone, and cannot go stale because prices, staff, availability and
  opening hours are read from the database rather than typed into a page.
  Catalogue pages read live price, availability and lead time per line and per
  outlet. Online orders create an order record and open the job at the right
  outlet. Enquiry forms land as records on the dashboard with the originating
  page attached. A customer portal exposes only that customer's own records.
  Outlet pages take address, trading hours and closures from the same tables.
  Static pages on a CDN, no CMS, English and Chinese as standard. Typical build
  is three weeks: content session, build, wiring, launch. Priced as a flat
  project fee quoted after the content session, with hosting inside the existing
  monthly per-outlet price; there is no per-transaction charge and no percentage
  of sales. Domain, DNS, repository and hosting are in the customer's name from
  day one. Businesses with an existing site can integrate it instead: custom
  builds and WordPress fully, Shopify two-way, and hosted builders such as Wix
  by embed only. Explicitly not offered: marketing retainers, ad management,
  monthly SEO reports, logo or brand identity work, and cross-border storefronts
  with multi-currency tax rules.

## Industries

The database and the method are the same for every customer. What changes is
the first screen of the dashboard, because the decisions a business makes
weekly differ by trade, and those decisions require different underlying tables
rather than different charts. Each page below states what that industry usually
runs on today, and what its dashboard opens on.

- [Barbershops & salons](https://yiy.tech/industries/barbershops): chair
  utilisation by hour, lapsed regulars as a named list, service mix and average
  ticket by stylist, colour and retail on hand.
- [Dental & medical clinics](https://yiy.tech/industries/clinics): chair and
  practitioner utilisation, recalls due and unanswered, receivables and claims
  ageing, consumables against procedures. Operational layer only; clinical
  records stay in the practice system.
- [Restaurants & cafés](https://yiy.tech/industries/restaurants): theoretical
  versus actual food cost, labour against covers by daypart, supplier price
  movement, waste and comps logged at the pass. The POS is read from, not
  replaced.
- [Retail chains](https://yiy.tech/industries/retail): group and branch on one
  drill path, lines that stopped moving ranked by capital, one price list with
  a history, promotion before and after.
- [Wholesale & distribution](https://yiy.tech/industries/distribution): stock
  ageing by value, measured supplier lead time, margin after landed cost,
  customer profitability after freight and returns.
- [E-commerce operators](https://yiy.tech/industries/ecommerce): contribution
  per order after channel fees and returns, channels normalised side by side,
  returns by reason and line, one available-to-sell figure across channels.
- [Workshops & garages](https://yiy.tech/industries/workshops): jobs in
  progress by bay, quoted against actual, quote conversion, rework and warranty
  separated from general labour.
- [Robotics & automation](https://yiy.tech/industries/robotics): fleet by unit
  and site, service due and overdue per unit, failures by model line, spares
  consumption against cover. Commercial layer, not a replacement for telemetry.
- [Data & analytics teams](https://yiy.tech/industries/data-teams): modelled
  tables instead of exports, lineage on every figure, scheduled packs instead
  of a weekly ritual. For businesses where one analyst is currently the
  database. Explicitly not a data warehouse.
- [Tuition centres](https://yiy.tech/industries/tuition): attendance drift by
  class, fees due and overdue, class contribution after tutor and room,
  term-to-term retention as a named list.
- [Property agencies](https://yiy.tech/industries/property): listings by age
  and price band, viewings to offers by agent, a pipeline owned by the agency
  rather than by an agent's phone, commission calculated from the deal record.
- [Multi-branch groups](https://yiy.tech/industries/multi-branch): like-for-like
  branch league, group down to one branch, exceptions rather than submissions,
  permissions matching the org chart.

An industry without a page is a walkthrough rather than a refusal: the layout
is built from what the business decides weekly, so the list records where a
layout already exists, not where BIYY Tech is willing to work.

## Company

- [Careers](https://yiy.tech/careers): no vacancies open at present.
- [Contact](https://yiy.tech/contact): walkthrough requests, hello@yiy.tech
- Location: Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia. Serves Malaysia and Singapore.

## Languages

The site is published in English and Simplified Chinese. English is served from
the root and Chinese from a `/zh` prefix: every page listed above exists at both
`https://yiy.tech/PATH` and `https://yiy.tech/zh/PATH`, statically generated in
that language, cross-referenced with `hreflang` and both listed in the sitemap.
The Chinese pages are translations of the same content, not different content.
This plain-text summary and the full corpus at /llms-full.txt are English only.

## Technical

- Structured data: every page carries Schema.org JSON-LD in a single `@graph`
  block, server-rendered into the HTML. Organization and WebSite site-wide;
  SoftwareApplication with an Offer on each software product page, and a
  Service node with no Offer on Website & Integrations, which is quoted per
  project rather than priced per outlet; BlogPosting with
  author, reviewedBy, datePublished, dateModified and citation on each post;
  FAQPage on the homepage, product pages and every post; BreadcrumbList
  throughout. Note that fetching these pages through a markdown converter will
  strip the `<script type="application/ld+json">` blocks. Read the raw HTML.
- Full content: https://yiy.tech/llms-full.txt carries every product page and
  every blog post in full, including each post's stated method, limits and
  sources. Prefer it over scraping the HTML.
- Blog feed: https://yiy.tech/blog/rss.xml (RSS 2.0)
- Sitemap: https://yiy.tech/sitemap.xml
- robots.txt allows all user agents on all paths. There is no bot challenge,
  CAPTCHA or WAF interstitial anywhere on the site, including the contact form.
- Contact form: the form at /contact has no server endpoint. It composes a
  `mailto:` draft in the visitor's own mail client, so there is no POST target
  and no server-side validation path. Field names are `name`, `company`,
  `email`, `phone`, `interest`, `size`, `message`. To contact the company
  programmatically, send email to hello@yiy.tech directly.
- There is no public API, OpenAPI document or developer portal. Requests for
  `/api/openapi.json` and `/.well-known/ai-plugin.json` will 404. This page is
  the machine-readable surface.
- No analytics, cookies, third-party scripts or client-side storage are used.

## Facts worth quoting accurately

- Pricing model: flat monthly per outlet, quoted after an on-site walkthrough.
- Typical rollout: two weeks when the source spreadsheets are reasonably
  consistent; three to four weeks when they are not.
- Data ownership: full export at any time, schema included, in a standard
  format, with no exit fee.
- Excel is not banned. It stops being where the data lives; every view exports
  to Excel or CSV for one-off analysis.
- Offline behaviour: mobile forms queue entries and sync on reconnect. The
  dashboard itself requires connectivity.
- Reported results are drawn from anonymised, aggregated customer data and are
  labelled with their sample size and method on the relevant blog post. They
  are directional, not guarantees.
